wolfram.note: I * Infinity evaluates to ComplexInfinity before Argument sees it, so the direction is lost and Argument answers Indeterminate; Wolfram's DirectedInfinity[I] has argument Pi/2. The same cause as ExpIntegralEi at +-I Infinity.
sage.note: Sage leaves arg(I*Infinity) held; ours answers Indeterminate where Wolfram and SymPy answer pi/2.
mpmath.note: mpmath keeps the direction of i·∞ (as Wolfram does), so arg is π/2; ours reads it as ~oo, which has no argument. compute-engine keeps one complex infinity, ~oo, and no directed one (cortex-js/compute-engine#396: arnog kept the type error at boxing, one ~oo and no directed infinity; our PR #401 was closed to align).
julia.note: compute-engine answers "Indeterminate", which an arb ball cannot represent (it has no infinite point, and its NaN does not tell a pole from an undefined value or lost precision), so Julia's non-finite ball says nothing about it.
